characters.name: Ren Höek
characters.description: An "Asthma Hound" Chihuahua prone to psychotic breakdowns and acts of violence. Whatever he does, expect for it to be somehow materially motivated,but he's still good friendswithStimpy. In fact, Stimpy might be theonlyfriend he has. Adaptational Villainy: He was hardly a nice guy in the original show, butAdult Party Cartoonramps up his negative traits while reducing or outright excising his good ones. He does show a few more sincere moments of friendship towards Stimpy, however, a redeeming quality that was often lost in the Games episodes. All Men Are Perverts: Just watch "Naked Beach Frenzy," and you'll know what we mean. Ambiguously Bi:Word of Godsays Ren likes human women, but "when you look like Ren, you take what you can get". Anti-Role Model: With how mean, deranged, and self-serving he can be, he's obviously not a model example of how people should behave. Stimpy thinks otherwise, though (but then, he's Stimpy...).

characters.name: Stimpson "Stimpy" J. Cat
characters.description: Stimpy is anoverweight Manx catwith no...er, well, let's say"little" brains and a big heart.He is friends with Ren, despite having to deal with Ren'sinsanityand violencecomically or not, he manages to put up witheverythingand isin good-spirits. Acrofatic: Despite being a fat and bloated eediot, Stimpy is seen many times to bounce at high speeds to match with show's fast-paced,Clampett-inspredanimation style. Some notable examples include Stimpy jumping during the Muddy Mudskipper song from "Stimpy's Big Day" and Stimpy hopping haphazardly to his "appointment" from "Sven Hoek". All-Loving Hero: He does not dislike anybody. In fact, he is never mad at Ren despite how much the latter is mean to him. Ambiguously Bi: While he is a couple with Ren in theAdult Party Cartoonseries, the original series showed instances of him being interested in women, even if they weren't as common as Ren's. The first episode "Stimpy's Big Day"/"The Big Shot" shows him as a chick magnet after becoming famous, he and Ren are shown to have wives in "A Visit to Anthony" and "The House of Next Tuesday" has Stimpy use a gadget to envision himself surrounded by sexy women. In addition, the episode "I Love Chicken" has him fall in love with a chicken he was supposed to cook for Ren's dinner and regard her as a female, whilethe goat head he falls for at the end of the episodeis indicated to be male by the goat head wearing a top hat while Stimpy's in a wedding dress. Ascended Fanboy: In 'Stimpy's Big Day', he wins a poem writing contest for the chance to meet Muddy Mudskipper, and becomes a big star in Hollywood, doing all sorts of TV shows and commercials, all despite Ren's "cartoons will ruin your mind" rants.

characters.name: Mr. Horse
characters.description: Mr. Horse is perhaps theOnly Sane Man. But he might be theAx-Crazyone, too. He was a doctor, a psychologist,note"Psychologist? Are you nuts?" He's a horse!a psychically unbalanced creep, a war hero, a spokesman for the United Nations, an airplane pilot and many, many more. Who knows what he really is? Ascended Extra: While he is largely a gag character in the original show, his two appearances inAdult Party Cartoon("Ren Seeks Help" and "Stimpy's Pregnant") are more integral to the plot. Catchphrase: "No sir, I don't / didn't like it." Deadpan Snarker: At times. A Dog Named "Dog": A horse named "Mr. Horse".

characters.name: George Liquor, American
characters.description: George Liquor is an American so conservative that he thinks Republicans are communists. However, that part of his character was expanded in his own cartoon,The Goddamn George Liquor ProgramandSpümcø Comic Book- inThe Ren & Stimpy Show, he's portrayed as a man with a strong faith in rules and discipline. He only made two appearances on the show due to theNickelodeonexecs' absolute condemnation for the character and willingness to let John K. keep the rights to the character after he was fired from the show. Abhorrent Alpha Male: An arrogantManly Manwho is condescending at best and abusive at worst to those he views as "wimps". Adaptational Nice Guy: In hisRen & Stimpyoutings, George is a cruel, abusive authority figure who would aggressively exploit his subordinates to get his way, ironically considering these to be expressions of love. In further appearances, such asThe Goddamn George Liquor ProgramandWeekend Pussy Hunt, however, he's abrash, but good-hearted unclewho shows genuine care for his nephews, especially Jimmy the Idiot Boy, whom he is very protective of.However, in his latest appearance,Cans Without Labels,he's right back to his old abusive ways, with his nephews, Ernie and Slab, instead getting the short end of the stick. However, in his latest appearance,Cans Without Labels,he's right back to his old abusive ways, with his nephews, Ernie and Slab, instead getting the short end of the stick. Ax-Crazy: He's almost to Ren's extent of being insanely belligerent.

characters.name: Victor and Victor's dad
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: Victor, for Ren and Stimpy. Big Bad: Victor is probably the closest thing to the show's main antagonist. The Bully: Like father, like son. Card-Carrying Villain: Victor is indeed aware of himself being a bully and even carries a card with him being a certified bully on it. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Victor's dad was disappointed in Victor for giving Stimpy the Christmas underwear his mother lovingly stitched.

characters.name: Powdered Toast Man
characters.description: Adam Westing: It's Gary Owens using hisSpace Ghostvoice. Badass Preacher: His secret identity is that of a "cool youth deacon." Breakout Character: He started out as a segment. Also, he's the most likelyRen and Stimpycharacter to appear in crossover games after the duo themselves. Catchphrase: He frequently exclaims "Leave everything to me!" and "POWDEEEEEEEEEEERED TOOOOOOOAAAAST MAAAAAAAAAAAN!" Catholic School Girls Rule: His assistant and implied love interest appears to be a voluptuous Catholic schoolgirl.

characters.name: Muddy Mudskipper
characters.description: Alliterative Name:MuddyMudskipper. Catchphrase: "Ya lousy bum." Everyone Has Standards: In "Ren Needs Help!", he is appalled when Ren admits he smacks Stimpy. Institutional Apparel: In "Dinner Party", he gets an invitation to Ren's dinner party while in prison and is shown wearing a striped convict uniform. Interspecies Romance: In "Jerry the Bellybutton Elf", he brings his human girlfriend to a party, where she promptly eats all the clam dip. Later episodes show his newest wife is an ape.

characters.name: Mr. Pipe
characters.description: The Faceless: Though one episode showed a silhouette of his face. Fan Disservice: Do we really need to see his skinny, hairy legs all the time? Gasshole: He randomly rips a fart at least once per appearance. Parental Substitute: To Ren and Stimpy in "Big Baby Scam." Ugly Guy, Hot Wife: He could have ahandsome face we're not seeingbut otherwise.

characters.name: Mrs. Pipe
characters.description: Blind Driving: While she's driving an RV in "Road Apples", we see in the rear view mirror reflection that her eyes are closed. Collector of the Strange: Dirty diapers. The Faceless: Although we do see the back of her blond head while she drives an RV in "Road Apples". Housewife: Her overall aesthetic is that of a 1950s housewife. Ms. Fanservice: Though wenever see her facewhat we do see of her body is attractive in a "1950s housewife" way.

characters.name: The Fire Chief
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: As a dutiful fire-fighting hero, he has nothing but psychotic hatred for those public threats, circus midgets. Pity that those appalling apparitions appear everywhere and aseveryone. With his trusty shovel thankfully he will take care of them as the beating of HaggisMcHaggisand the torture of Ren and Stimpy when they were dressed up as clowns, demonstrates. Berserk Button: He really hates circus midgets. Catchphrase: "I've had it UP TO HEEEEEEERE WITH THE LIKES OF YOU PEOPLE!! (Beat) Oh! I'm sorry, I thought you were circus midgets." The Cuckoolander Was Right: In "Ren Needs Help", he makes the deranged claim that the President is fake, is put in a fake suit and makes speeches on the moon. It later turns out that this nonsense has a grain of truth to it when the episode ends with a lobotomized Ren dressed to look like the President and filmed on the moon to make his national address. Large Ham: Especially chews the scenery when ranting about his dislike of circus midgets.

characters.name: It's That Man Again
characters.description: A smarmy, overly-enthusiastic travelling salesman who occasionally crosses paths with Ren and Stimpy. He also serves as the announcer for the Captain Höek cartoons. Ambiguously Human: Early appearances had him with a antennae sticking out of his head. Honest John's Dealership: He seems to sell all manner of items. Large Ham: Has aNO INDOOR VOICE. Master of Disguise: Once inexplicably transformed into a slice of toast.

characters.name: Abner Dimwitt and Ewalt Nitwitt
characters.description: Annoying Laugh: Their laughter consists of snorting and weird throaty "yuk" sounds. The Ditz: They ain't called "Dimwitt" and "Nitwitt" for nothin'. Good Ol' Boy: They're Southern folk who mean well in spite of not being very smart. Jeopardy! Thinking Music: When they think, a pastiche of theJeopardy!theme song plays. Meaningful Name: Their surnames are "Dimwitt" and "Nitwitt" and they are both dumb.

characters.name: Kowalski
characters.description: Dumb Muscle: He isverybuff andverystupid. Enfant Terrible: He's seven years old and in prison forcrimes against humanity. Fat Idiot: It's more muscle than fat, but he's still dumb. Hair-Trigger Temper: He violently lashes out when frustrated, such as the time heatomizeda sofa and a television set with his bare hands, then did the same thing to Stimpy. Hulk Speak: He's not very articulate."Daddy hit baby! Baby mad!"

characters.name: Wilbur Cobb
characters.description: A former cartoon producer, first introduced in "Stimpy's Cartoon", to whom the years have not been kind. He showed up in a few other shorts as a stock "rambling, crazy old man" character. Body Horror: In "Stimpy's Cartoon", we see a hermit crab crawl into his head, his ear falls off and when he takes off his glasses, his eyes and nose come off with them. Worst of all is when his arms tear off after getting his hands stuck to his desk. Cloudcuckoolander: Half the time, he's rambling incoherently about subjects in a way that he appears to have no idea what he's talking about. It scares Ren and Stimpy. False Teeth Tomfoolery: He is sometimes depicted as wearing dentures, which often fail to stay in his mouth. Killed Off for Real: Dies at the end of "Galoot Wranglers" afterTempting Fateby saying "may I drop dead." However, he still makes one last appearance as an angel in heaven in "The Last Temptation".

characters.name: The Shaven Yak
characters.description: The Big Guy: He's very large and strong. You Mean "Xmas": He's the gift-giver of a Christmas-like holiday called Yak-Yak Shaving Day.

characters.name: Mrs. Buttloaves
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: Most of the episodes where she appears have her showing interest in Ren. Badass Bystander: In "Fire Dogs", when she sees Ren's passed out on the ladder after seeing how high up he is, she takes it upon herself to get him back down. She grabs him in his teeth and descends the ladder, and then tries to give Ren CPR as thanks for trying to help her. Big Beautiful Woman: The severed head inBellhopscertainly sees her as such. Gonk: One of the show's ugliest characters. Gross-Up Close-Up: We're treated withthis grotesque close up of her◊after she resituates Ren in "Fire Dogs".

characters.name: Stinky Wizzleteats
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: He's clearly a very weird fellow, if certain parts of the Happy Happy Joy Joy Song are any indication. Large Ham: "I TOLD YOU I'D SHOOT, BUT YOU DIDN'T BELIEVE ME!WHY DIDN'T YOU BELIEVE ME?!" No Celebrities Were Harmed:Burl Ives. Pseudo-Santa: "A Scooter for Yaksmas" depicts him as being the Ren and Stimpy universe's equivalent to Santa Claus.

characters.name: Old Man Hunger
characters.description: Art Evolution: His cameo in theAdult Party Cartoonepisode "Altruists" gives him a pointier beard, a thin mustache, wilder hair at his temples, a bluer and more bulbous nose and replaces the drumstick on his head with an ice cream cone. Part of the reason for this change in design is because the cameo repurposes him as a representation of Old Man Winter. Artifact Name: He's called Old Man Hunger because he first appeared in the pilot as anAnthropomorphic Personificationof Ren and Stimpy's starvation for a briefVisual Gagto represent the narrator's mention of Old Man Hunger nibbling at the duo's bellies. His subsequent appearances don't have anything to do with food or eating, with hisAdult Party Cartoonappearance even repurposing him as a representation of Old Man Winter. Ascended Extra: He initially appeared as a minor gag character in the "Big House Blues" pilot, "Big Baby Scam" and "Ren's Toothache" before having a marginally more significant role in "The Great Outdoors". Cloudcuckoolander: "The Great Outdoors" has him repeatedly exclaim his love of doing things in the nude. Dirty Old Man: If going around nude isn't enough, watch the episodes he is in.

characters.name: HaggisMcHaggis
characters.description: Asshole Victim: Gets beaten up by the fire chief after tearing up his son's favourite pair of undies. Ax-Crazy: Finds humour in beating up his dog. Baldness Angst: "A Hard Day's Luck" has him unhappy about being bald and hoping that the leprechaun will grant his wish of having hair. Barbie Doll Anatomy: The one time we see up his kilt in "Scotsman in Space", we see he has no nethers. Berserk Button: In "Scotsman in Space", he gets extremely irate over Ren and Stimpy overcooking his eggs and serving him haggis without chutney.

characters.name: Svën Höek
characters.description: Ren's dimwitted cousin from Scandinavia. Ascended Extra: He only made one prominent appearance besides the odd brief cameo, but appeared more often in the Marvel Comic book. Collector of the Strange: He collects Band-Aids and spit. The Ditz: He's an "eediot" like Stimpy, which is one of the ways they get along so quickly. Dogs Are Dumb: He's a dog and is a lot stupider than Stimpy. His character design sheet even describes him as being "even more stupid than Stimpy".

characters.name: Reverend Jack Cheese
characters.description: A meat-worshipping reverend. Only appears in the episode "Reverend Jack". Captain Ersatz: A crazy, arrogant, obsessive villain with a bizarre fashion sense and the voice of Frank Gorshin? Sounds an awful lot likeThe Riddlerto us. Knuckle Tattoos: The reverend has tattoos grafted on his hands, with one saying "PITY" and the other "SELF PITY". Large Ham: This is what happens when you invite the famously over-the-top Frank Gorshin to guest star on a show as crazy as this. Parody Religion: "We are gathered here today to pay homage to MEAT!"

characters.name: Jerry the Bellybutton Elf
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: When he is given lintloaf, he becomes very insane and violent. Berserk Button: Whatever you do, donotserve him lintloaf. Cyclops: In his elf form, he only has one eye. Disney Acid Sequence: "Climb Inside My World". Disproportionate Retribution: He attempts tomurderStimpy just because the latter gave him lintloaf.Misplaced Retribution: Extends his wrath to Ren despite him not being involved in any way.

characters.name: Sarge
characters.description: Drill Sergeant Nasty: Quite persuasive especially with a tank gun at his disposal. Large Ham: Somehow manages to extend a nine-letter word into a sixty-seven one."A-TEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEENNNNNNNNNNNNNN-HOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOT!!!!!!!!!!"

characters.name: Brainchild
characters.description: Child Prodigy: He lives up to his name by being a child genius. Dark Is Not Evil: He may be a bit creepy-looking, but he does manage to help Ren get Stimy out of a constant state of destructive stupidity. Mad Scientist: He blows Stimpy up so that Ren can travel inside him and find out what's ceasing his brain activity, plus he appears to have experimented on his own mother. My Brain Is Big: He's highly intelligent and he has a very large head.

characters.name: The Ghost
characters.description: Back from the Dead: At the end of the episode, he drinks poison and it somehow resurrects him as a black man. Driven to Suicide: He's already dead to begin with, but when he gives up on trying to scare the duo, he drinks a bottle of poison to try anyway—and inexplicably comes back to life as a jolly fat black guy,who promptly drives off in a convertible. Ineffectual Sympathetic Villain: Not exactly villainous of sorts, but he is pretty hapless at getting so much as a look of surprise out of Ren and Stimpy. No Name Given: He's not given an actual name.

characters.name: Charles Globe
characters.description: Hard Work Hardly Works: He admits that his well-proportioned torso wasn't a result of working out, but from having the excess fat in his legs surgically transplanted. Hunk: Once you get past the fact that his head is a globe, he's pretty impressive. Informed Attribute: While Stimpy introduces him as a fitness guru, he's never worked out a day in his life. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's a lazier version of Charles Atlas.

characters.name: Waffle Woman
characters.description: Alliterative Name: Her first and last name start with a "W". Evil Is Petty: She blew up chunks on the world because her liquid waffles didn't sell as well as powdered toast. We Will Meet Again: After Powdered Toast Man defeats her, she vows that she'll have her revenge right before she floats off into space. Yandere: During her last fight with Powdered Toast Man, both drop hints of being bitter ex-lovers.

characters.name: Sammy Mantis
characters.description: Early-Bird Cameo: Before his introduction, he has a minor appearance in the episode "Dinner Party". No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's obviously based off ofSammy Davis Jr.

characters.name: The Frog
characters.description: Appears in "Ren Seeks Help". Ate His Gun: At the end of "Ren Seeks Help", he attempts suicide this way with Mr. Horse's gun. However, once he pulls the trigger, it turns out that it was agag gun, keeping him alive and in even more misery than before. Butt-Monkey: He is was tortured by Ren in many brutal ways such as ramming him with his bike until he squeezed his guts out, setting him on fire with car battery etc. Death Seeker: Wants Ren to put it out of its misery after all the suffering Ren put it through but Renrefuses to so even after his parents order him to. Driven to Suicide: After years of pain and misery due to Ren refusing to kill him, he decides to take matters into his own hands and attempt to blow his brains out with Mr. Horse's gun. It doesn't work.

characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Höek
characters.description: Ren's parents, whom we see in his flashbacks in "Ren Seeks Help". Adam Westing: Mr. Höek is voiced by John K's actual father, whom the character is partially based on. Artistic License – Religion: Mr. Höek is a Catholic priest, even though members of that priesthood are sworn to celibacy. While it's admittedly possible that he was breaking the rules, the fact that he doesn't seem to be making any effort to hide the fact that he's in a romantic and sexual relationship makes it hard to believe he could get away with it. Ax-Crazy: Given how hostile they are towards each other, combined with them being perfectly fine with handing their son dangerous weapons without supervision, you can tell the apple doesn't fall far from the tree. Bait-and-Switch: When Mr. Höek explains to Ren that torturing the frog is wrong, he pulls out a giant Bible, implying that he plans on resolving the issue peacefully, but when he opens it, it's revealed that there is aguninside, then he gives Ren the gun and orders him tokill the frog with it.Mrs. Höek also plays a part in this trope, as right after this, she furiously calls out and pistol whips her husband for giving Ren the gun, making the audience believe thatshe'llbe the one to set things right, before she happily hands Ren achainsawto kill the frog with instead.

characters.name: Ralph Bakshi
characters.description: Yes, THATRalph Bakshi. He appears solely in "Fire Dogs II", with Ren and Stimpy hanging out with him. Adam Westing: Yes, that really is Bakshi voicing himself. Ax-Crazy: LITERALLY! When he has a nightmare about Circus Midgets, he wildly swings an axe around his bedroom, nearly killing the main duo. Big Fun: A big fat guy who's rather eccentric but friendly. Body Horror: He was originally the Fire Chief, but he inexplicably morphs into Bakshi before our very eyes.

characters.name: The Lifeguard
characters.description: Carpet of Virility: He's more hair than man. Gag Penis: Has a visible bulge in his trunks. Hero Antagonist: Ren sexually harassing girls on the beach makes an enemy of this guy. Lantern Jaw of Justice: He's got a massive chin and is for the most part the hero of the episode. Naked People Are Funny: He rips off his trunks so he can use them as a weapon against Ren and stays naked for the rest of the episode.
